A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the symmetric phase the baryon asymmetry is produced by sphalerons at a rate which is about 20-25% smaller than the pure gauge theory rate, while in the broken phase the rate is about the same.
the sphaleron transition rate in the symmetric (and broken) phases is reduced by about 20% by the Higgs field.
the sphaleron transition rate is reduced by the Higgs bosons, but the reduction is small, of the order of 20%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sphaleron rates in the symmetric phase are not much larger than the rates in the broken phase, and that this conclusion is not affected by the Higgs bosons.
the sphaleron rates in the symmetric phase of the Standard Model and in pure Yang-Mill theory are very similar.
the sphaleron transition rate is a very good probe of the electroweak symmetry breaking mechanism.
